abstract.para: smartmontools (S.M.A.R.T. Monitoring Tools) is a software suite used to control and monitor storage systems using the Self-Monitoring, Analysis and Reporting Technology (S.M.A.R.T.) built into modern ATA, SATA, SCSI, SAS and NVMe hard drives and solid-state drives. It plays a critical role in early disk failure detection and hardware monitoring.

topic.para: The smartmontools packages follow the stable lifecycle model. They are updated and supported according to the following rules:

listitem.para: smartmontools is categorized under the stable lifecycle because upstream versions maintain strict backward compatibility. This ensures that updates do not introduce disruptive changes or affect existing system configurations, script integrations or reliability.

To perform new hardware enablement and support new storage drive models, we may update the smartmontools version. Because upstream releases preserve backward compatibility, updates are primarily driven by new features and hardware support requested by customers that are difficult or impractical to backport.
When a new version with useful features or new hardware support is available upstream, the packages are updated across all supported codestreams in active maintenance.

Since the upstream release schedule is irregular, new version submissions are permitted as they are released upstream. These updates can be delivered either within a new &suselinux; minor release or directly as part of maintenance updates for already released codestreams.
